text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every task. In supervised learning, the most common approach, we give the computer a set of training data. This data includes examples with known answers, like photos labeled as "cat" or "dog." The computer uses this data to build a model, which is essentially a set of rules or patterns it discovers. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. For example, after learning from labeled photos, it can guess whether a new picture shows a cat or a dog. Finally, we test the model's accuracy by comparing its predictions to the correct answers, helping us see how well it has learned.
